tagline: Twelve miles up to a gold town that kept its buildings.
intro: About 30 miles east of Missoula the Garnet Range Road leaves Highway 200 and climbs 2,000 feet in 12 miles through evergreen forest. At the top, around 6,000 feet in First Chance Gulch, is Garnet.

Miners worked these mountains from the 1860s, and when a stamp mill went up in 1895 a town grew around it, with three hotels, grocery stores, a barber shop and close to thirteen saloons. The gold gave out and the people left. Thirty buildings stayed, and they look much as they did in 1895.

moments.title: Garnet Range Road
moments.text: As the road climbs, the Blackfoot River valley opens up behind it, with the Swan Range, the Mission Mountains and the Bob Marshall Wilderness beyond.

moments.title: Garnet
moments.text: The hotels charged one to three dollars a night, and a miner who could not manage that could sleep in a windowless attic for a quarter.

practical: In winter the byway is closed to cars and groomed for snowmobiles, and the other way in, up Bear Gulch from I-90, is steep, narrow and rough and not recommended for trailers or RVs.
